Negotiation as a tactic of war or a tool in the service of peace? Mohammad-Baqer Qalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, has repeated for the umpteenth time that "we fight and we negotiate." Yes. There is no contradiction between war and negotiation such that one would be forced to choose between the two. But what is meant by negotiation? Is negotiation a tool for achieving peace and ending hostility? Or is it a tactic to create opportunities and buy time to prepare and be better equipped to continue the war? If the second meaning is intended, then constructing the war-negotiation duality is pointless, because in that case negotiation amounts to nothing more than a tactic of war. But if what is meant by negotiation is ending the war and achieving peace, then the war-peace duality is a more logical substitute for the war-negotiation duality. War and peace, however, unlike war and negotiation, are contradictory and cannot be reconciled; therefore one must inevitably choose one of them. In my view, our country has now reached a point where it must inevitably choose between war and peace. Mr. Qalibaf, as the head of Iran's negotiating team, is obliged to face public opinion on this matter with greater candor and courage. The conceptualization of terms is the responsibility of Mr. Qalibaf and other officials who speak about this. Words and expressions without conceptualization are like balloons full of air—more useful for entertainment than for conveying a message and clarifying a goal! The political atmosphere of our country has become so swollen from the sheer volume and accumulation of unconceptualized words that everyone is dazed and confused! #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

Against Sheikh Hassan or Sheikh Ahmad? These nights, at street gatherings, some speakers are making claims about Sheikh Hassan Rouhani that, in this sorrowful situation, bring comfort to people's hearts and a smile to their lips! The late Seyyed Ebrahim Nabavi is sorely missed! If he were alive, he would have had fresh material for satire! Perhaps if that departed soul had imagined such material would be created for him, he wouldn't have been in such a hurry to depart for the eternal realm! This Sheikh Hassan Rouhani, according to one speaker at the nightly gatherings, is apparently so sensitive to heat that he can't tolerate the normal temperature of the governor's office in Mashhad for even a few minutes! As if he weren't a child of Sorkheh on the edge of the scorching desert! Anyone who didn't know better would think he must be from Kuhin or Yush or Si-Sakht, or Olas-Belanga, or Bileh-Darreh, or Jahan-Nama or Gajereh or Khalkhal or Gaduk — a mountain pass of Khuneh-Sorkh — who can't endure a moment of heat! But the speakers at the nightly gatherings are beating a dead horse with these words, because any fault or flaw they attribute to former presidents also lands squarely on the members of the Guardian Council they hold dear! Every elementary school child in this country knows that presidential elections here are held in two stages. That is, first the Guardian Council selects a number from among dozens and sometimes hundreds of candidates and passes them through the filter of its supervision, and then the people vote for one of those selected. The Guardian Council's selection, unlike in many countries, is not a formality or based merely on verifying the apparent qualifications and civil identity and birth certificate of presidential candidates, but rather it is a matter of approbatory supervision according to its own particular definition, such that it must establish in the candidate such qualities as being a capable manager and prudent, of good record, trustworthy, pious, faithful, and believing in the foundations of the Islamic Republic of Iran and the official religion of the country — so thoroughly that not a hair's breadth of fault can be found. Sheikh Hassan Rouhani was approved for qualification not once but twice by Sheikh Ahmad Jannati and the majority of his fellow jurists and legal scholars on the Guardian Council to run in the presidential elections, and all the above qualities in him were confirmed by Mr. Jannati and his colleagues. After that, the people voted for him! Therefore, in terms of logic, any attribution of impiety to Mr. Rouhani is automatically a strike through the understanding and knowledge and ability and qualification of the majority of the jurists and legal scholars of the Guardian Council, especially Sheikh Ahmad Jannati! If this is what the speakers at the nightly gatherings want, let them carry on! #Ahmad_Zaidabadi @ahmadzeidabad
